instrument_correction.fault: fieldRadius() returned the FIRST centred circle over r 35 in document order. instrument_correction.the_tell_that_was_missed: v1 printed "% outside field" and "% outside disc" (the latter hardcoded at 47) side by side, and on exactly the penny and the nickel the two columns came out BIT-IDENTICAL. Spec 4 says in as many words that two bit-identical answers from two different inputs is not agreement. The evidence was in round 0's own console output and the judge did not read it.

The field circle is the SMALLEST centred circle over r 35; the choice is audited rather than assumed — every candidate is collected and printed beside the result, and the run THROWS if the non-blank candidates disagree or if "smallest" and "not the blank" disagree. Measured: the darkest pixel available in the ring band, per 0.5 degree, at DEVICE resolution — the quarter reverse at 54px goes from 31 washed-out angles of 720 to 30, and the lightest sample is IDENTICAL (197 at 223.0 deg) before and after.

looked_at.what_did_change: a real, smaller thing, and in the right direction. At 54px on the quarter reverse there was white bevel spill on the REEDED RIM just OUTSIDE the field ring, at 200-204 deg (about 9.7 o clock), reaching grey 221 against a rim median of 197. In round 1 the maximum on that circle equals the median exactly — the spill is gone. The obverse never had it, in either revision, which is what attributes it to the bevel rather than to the specular arc.
looked_at.honest_note: on first reading the 54px crop I believed I saw the ring break and heal, because I had been told it would. The device-resolution ring walk and the obverse control are what corrected me. An impression from a nearest-upscaled tile is exactly what spec 8 warns about, and it caught me before it caught anyone else.
